description:
**File**: `src/websocket/event_broadcaster.cr:99-118`

**Severity**: P2 (mutex contention, leaky abstraction per architecture.md)

`broadcast_json` holds `@@mutex` for the entire iteration of
`@@clients` and `@@subscribers`. Each `client.send(json)` is a
network IO operation that runs inside the global mutex.

A slow client blocks `EventBroadcaster.stats`, `subscribe`,
`unsubscribe`, and the entire broadcast loop — every other client
and every other subscriber has to wait for the slow client.

This violates `planning/architecture.md` §1 ("Hide implementation
details") because the broadcaster exposes the locking strategy
through its slow path; a caller cannot reason about latency without
understanding the internal locking.

**Fix sketch**:
1. Snapshot `@@clients.to_a` and `@@subscribers.to_a` inside the mutex
2. Release the mutex
3. Iterate the snapshot and perform the IO
4. Re-acquire the mutex only to remove failed clients/subscribers

Found during code review 2026-06-18, see
`planning/code-review-2026-06-18.md` §1.3.
title: EventBroadcaster holds @@mutex during client.send network IO
